BIOL2021 is targeted towards students interested in an in-depth introduction to cell biology. This course is reserved for Honors College students. Non-honors students will need to contact the instructor to request instructor’s permission (minimum GPA 3.5). This class fulfills BIOL majors and honors requirement. This course is offered in a hybrid format, combining weekly online lectures with required in-person 1hour discussions on Wednesday. Exams will be in-person in class. After all exams, students will give research presentations. Further details will be provided during the first week.

BIOL 3230 - 001 Developmental Biology

  • Class Number: 17496
  • Instructor: Gagnon, James
  • Teaching Assistant: Baldassari, Phil
  • Component: Lecture
  • Type: In Person
  • Units: 3.0
  • Requisites: Yes
  • Wait List: Yes
  • Seats Available: 49
This course will explore how a single fertilized egg gives rise to a complex, multicellular organism. Students will examine the genetic, molecular, and cellular mechanisms that control patterning, cell fate specification, morphogenesis, and organ formation, using model organisms to understand conserved developmental principles. Emphasis will be placed on experimental approaches from primary literature, including classical embryology, modern genomics, and imaging techniques, to connect fundamental mechanisms with evolution and human disease.

BIOL 5275 - 001 Microbial Biodiversity

  • Class Number:
  • Instructor: Dale, Colin
  • Teaching Assistant: Stohel, Izabel
  • Teaching Assistant: Sutherland, Alex
  • Component: Lecture
  • Type: In Person
  • Units: 4.0
  • Requisites: Yes
  • Wait List: Yes
  • Seats Available: -2
  • View Feedback
This course features a lecture component focusing on microbial diversity, genomics and evolution and an integrated "live" science laboratory class focusing on environmental microbiology, encompassing topics relevant to public health and basic microbiology. The course provides students with knowledge in microbial genomics and evolution and practical training in laboratory techniques including microbiology, molecular microbial identification and genomics, project management, data visualization and scientific presentation. This course requires registration for a lab and/or discussion section. Students will be automatically registered for this lecture section when registering for the pertinent lab and/or discussion section.

BIOL 5960 - 001 Experimental Genetics

  • Class Number: 2278
  • Instructor: Davis, Wayne W
  • Instructor: Jorgensen, Erik
  • Component: Special Topics
  • Type: In Person
  • Units: 3.0
  • Requisites: Yes
  • Wait List: Yes
  • Seats Available: 3
This course will focus on the context and fundamental experiments of genetics and molecular biology. In lectures, we will trace the foundation of genetics from Mendel’s experiments with peas through the determination of the structure of DNA and to how modern synthetic biology can be used to engineer organisms. In parallel, the laboratory sections of this course will use modern methods to recreate these classic experiments and train students in experimental design and best practices. Pre-requisite: BIOL 2020 or 2021. This course counts as an L2 lab in the Biology major. Please request a permission code here: https://www.biology.utah.edu/permission-codes/ This course is not available to students who took BIOL 3960 Spring 2023 or BIOL 5960 Fall 2023 or Fall 2024.

BIOL 5960 - 003 Plant Ecology Lab

  • Class Number: 17558
  • Instructor: Avila Lovera, Eleinis
  • Teaching Assistant: Gerstein, Vivian
  • Component: Special Topics
  • Type: In Person
  • Units: 1.0
  • Requisites: Yes
  • Wait List: Yes
  • Seats Available: 8
This laboratory course accompanies BIOL 5460 and provides hands-on experience with the concepts introduced in lecture. Students will engage in field- and lab-based investigations to explore plant ecological processes across environmental gradients. Activities include data collection, experimental design, and ecological measurements in local Wasatch Mountain ecosystems. Through these immersive experiences, students will deepen their understanding of plant–environment interactions, community dynamics, and ecological responses to environmental change. Corequisite: Biol5460. Please register by requesting a permission code here: https://www.biology.utah.edu/permission-codes/
